# [CS029] Hardcoded or Weak JWT Signing Secret (jwt-weak-secret)

A JWT is signed with a constant or short secret.

| | |
| --- | --- |
| **Severity** | HIGH |
| **Category** | Security |
| **CWE** | [CWE-326](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/326.html) |
| **OWASP** | A04:2025 |
| **Auto-Fix supported** | No |

## Why It Matters in Go

A secret in the source is visible to everyone with repository access, and short HMAC secrets can be brute-forced offline from a single token. Load at least 32 random bytes from a secret store.

## Vulnerable / Problematic Example

```go
signed, err := token.SignedString([]byte("secret"))
```

## Safe / Idiomatic Go Pattern

```go
signed, err := token.SignedString(signingKey) // 32+ random bytes from the secret store
```

## Configuration & Suppression

Disable the rule for the whole module in `.codexsentinel.yaml`:

```yaml
rules:
  disabled: [jwt-weak-secret]
```

Change its severity:

```yaml
rules:
  severity_overrides:
    jwt-weak-secret: low
```

Suppress one reviewed finding on its line, with the reason:

```go
//codex:ignore jwt-weak-secret -- <reason>
```

Or ignore it under a path in `.codexsentinel.ignore`:

```text
internal/legacy/** jwt-weak-secret
```
